verdict_reason: No actionable defects found in the reviewed native fixture. This source-only verdict does not qualify production integration or Phase 11A.
intent: Exercise distinct-UID private exchange through the actual Bifrost handler/core/local provider transport, concrete owner and capture clients, with synthetic route, authorization and services. No production qualification is claimed.
residual_risks: The fixture uses synthetic routing, provider, authorizer and broker/capture services; the services neither authenticate the gateway peer nor persist a real wallet ledger. It does not qualify production governance, durable custody or provider charge bounds.

Network isolation, capability limits, process boundary and exact teardown are supplied by the external launcher; on early failure the Go test does not join every child. Production watchdog and descendant cleanup remain unqualified.
The native fixture binary was not race-instrumented; prior component race tests cover narrower paths.
The fixture depends on normalizationHTTPAccount from the normalization test source; the composed installer must continue to include that test source.
testing_gaps: The positive fixture does not test denial under provider, owner or capture failure, or distinct-UID unauthorized peers in the joined path.
The fixture covers one synthetic answer route, not production middleware configuration, classifier, embedding, fallback, retries, daemon/host loss or recovery.

notes: Native fixture uses synthetic broker/capture ACKs; these servers do not verify gateway peer identity.
The external container launcher, not the Go test alone, establishes network isolation and exact teardown.
The native binary is not race instrumented.
The runtime fixture did not exercise production routing, real wallet, provider charge bounds or watchdog.
